Replay

Durable room removal

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Use rpc_remove(client, epoch, target_identity) to durably remove a member from a room. This optional authenticated extension lets only the current live authority disable another exact member/incarnation. Self-removal, stale epochs, changed incarnations, expired ownership and requests after release are refused. Trusted administration can still manage membership through coordinator_member.

Removal uses the existing Request/Reply layouts with separate envelope kinds 0x5203/0x5204 and separate HMAC domains. The Query-shaped payload contains only the epoch and target in successor; all other command fields must be zero. Normal Query remains Query, even with unused fields. Existing authority RPC schema, protocol version and durable record layouts remain unchanged. Old services ignore the new kind; callers must handle an unsupported-operation timeout.

The service stages the membership change and request frontier/result together and publishes them in one durable CAS. Disabling the nominated successor also clears its binding, prepared checkpoint and release state. An exact latest-request retry does not repeat the decision. Older requests cannot run after a newer read. Provisioned rooms use the same transaction as their enrollment bundle, so a service restart or old gameplay save cannot re-enable the removed enrollment.

Disabled keys can authenticate only a minimal denial, with zero remaining lease and no roster, endpoint or checkpoint disclosure. The response identifies only the requesting member as disabled and changes no durable frontier. Provisioning retains these keys in a separate denial-only table when reopening a room. They remain excluded from registration, rendezvous, checkpoint access and authority claims. Removal cannot retract checkpoint data already disclosed to a previously trusted participant.

Removal is durable for the room, not an account-wide ban or a proof that a person cannot acquire a separately authorized identity. It does not revoke outstanding invitations; applications must manage invite access separately.
